issues.title: Implement polyfit?
issues.body:
Fitting a line (or curve) to data along a specified axis is a long-standing need of xarray users. The main use case in my domain is finding the temporal trend on a 3D variable (e.g. temperature in time, lon, lat).

Yes, you can do it with apply_ufunc, but apply_ufunc is inaccessibly complex for many users. I am proposing we add a DataArray method called `polyfit`. It would work like this:

```python
da.polyfit(dim='time', deg=1)
```

returning the polynomial coefficients (and ideally covariance / residuals), with support for dask arrays.

issues.title: Create a ToC entry for every function, method, class, etc
issues.body:
It would be useful to have an option that causes Sphinx to automatically create a TOC entry for every function, class, and method. (In the absence of this, tables of contents are of limited value.)

Related: automodule places members under docstring headers. Whenever you use `.. automodule:: mod` with `:members:`, Sphinx inserts the module docstring, then inserts the members under that docstring. If the docstring contains headers, the functions are all placed under the bottommost header. This also affects the toctree, placing functions under module headers, which is not desired.

issues.title: quote qop options in Digest Auth
issues.body:
Based on RFC 2617 (http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2617), the value of the 'qop-options' directive in Digest Authentication should be quoted with double quotes:

> qop-options: If present, it is a quoted string of one or more tokens indicating the "quality of protection" values supported by the server. The value "auth" indicates authentication; the value "auth-int" indicates authentication with integrity protection.

Currently requests sends `qop=auth` unquoted, which violates the RFC and can break interoperability with some servers. The curl command-line tool also sends the qop value as a quoted string.

issues.title: url_for can't distinguish a blueprint mounted two times
issues.body:
Based on the blueprint concept, I expected relative `url_for` to work when the same blueprint is registered under two different url_prefixes:

```python
bp = Blueprint('foo', __name__)

@bp.route('/')
def func():
    return url_for('.func')

app = Flask(__name__)
app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix='/foo')
app.register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix='/bar')
```

Requesting `/foo/` and `/bar/` both return the URL of the first blueprint registered (`/foo/`). Is it possible to mount the same blueprint twice and make relative `url_for` resolve to the correct instance? Is this behaviour expected?

issues.title: Possibly move MessagesHandlerMixIn into PyLinter
issues.body:
### Current problem

The `MessagesHandlerMixIn` currently sits in its own module in the `pylint/message` directory. The class is always mixed into `PyLinter` except for one occasion where a class method is used. One of its most-used methods is `add_message`, which handles the messages added by all checkers.

This mixin pattern makes the type relationship between `MessagesHandlerMixIn` and `PyLinter` hard to express and reason about (mypy struggles with it). We should consider moving `MessagesHandlerMixIn` into `PyLinter` directly to simplify the class structure and typing.
